In Ethiopia, the Ministry of Health (MoH) has continued to provide strong leadership and coordination for the national immunization program. However, as the immunization landscape becomes increasingly complex, the program requires continuous analysis, evidence synthesis, and informed decision-making across multiple areas, including program improvement, new vaccine introduction, vaccine optimization, and policy development. To strengthen evidence-based decision-making in immunization, the Federal Ministry of Health established the Ethiopian National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (ENITAG) in 2016. ENITAG was formed with clear terms of reference through the appointment of independent national experts from diverse disciplines and the establishment of governance mechanisms to ensure transparency and effective management of conflicts of interest. WHO provided technical support during the establishment of ENITAG and has continued to support institutional capacity strengthening over the years. Since its establishment, ENITAG has produced several important recommendations and technical outputs that have guided the national immunization program and contributed to its recognition as a well-functioning NITAG. Nevertheless, independent WHO reviews conducted in 2023 identified several gaps, particularly related to the limited staffing and functionality of the Secretariat. In response, the MoH has prioritized strengthening the NITAG Secretariat as a key component of broader efforts to reinforce the national immunization program. title: Strengthening SUNCASA Evidence for GESI-Responsive Urban Nature-based Solutions: End-of-project evaluation
description: Background The Scaling Urban Nature-based Solutions for Climate Adaptation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SUNCASA) project aims to enhance climate resilience, gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and biodiversity protection across three cities: Dire Dawa (Ethiopia), Kigali (Rwanda), and Johannesburg (South Africa). This initiative is led by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) in partnership with the World Resources Institute, together with local partners. The main objective of SUNCASA is to address climate-induced risks (e.g., floods, landslides, and soil erosion) by implementing GESI-responsive nature-based solutions (NbS). This is aimed at strengthening the resilience of urban communities, watersheds, and biodiversity from the impacts of climate change, while reducing barriers to NbS participation among women and the underrepresented groups. This would be achieved through targeted interventions such as afforestation and reforestation programs, agroforestry, urban greening, and establishment of vegetated buffer zones in affected areas. The project was launched in late 2023, and implementation will be completed by late 2026. Despite growing interest and investment in urban NbS, relatively little evidence exists regarding how gender-responsive approaches to NbS influence project effectiveness, sustainability, governance, and equity outcomes. Gender-responsive approaches to NbS under SUNCASA are actions to protect, sustainably manage, and restore natural or modified ecosystems that address and challenge gender and social inequalities to promote equity, justice, and inclusion. This intersectional approach also considers diverse knowledge systems, including local knowledge, that result in equitable benefits from decision making and participation in NbS. As the project nears completion, SUNCASA offers a unique opportunity to strengthen the evidence base on how GESI-responsive NbS contribute to larger climate adaptation and biodiversity protection outcomes in urban contexts. To this end, IISD seeks to engage an external monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) consultancy team to conduct a theory-based end-of-project evaluation to assess progress toward achieving selected SUNCASA outcomes. The evaluation will employ theory-based mixed methods, such as key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs) for different sets of actors from each city. Deliverables of this opportunity will include a final external evaluation report (reporting against select outcomes) and communications products to showcase SUNCASA’s early impact/outcomes. Given the short project timeline of 3 years, this evaluation will focus on assessing evidence that supports the pathways of change hypothesized by SUNCASA and early signs of impact and sustainability from the project rather than looking for long-term impacts or effectiveness. This RFP outlines the scope, objectives, and deliverables for engaging a MEL consultancy team for evaluation data collection and final deliverables. Objective of the Assignment This evaluation will assess the end-of-project progress toward achievement of selected SUNCASA intermediate and immediate outcomes that targeted decision-makers and local implementing partners participating in the project. Using mixed methods, a theory-based final evaluation report (including thematic case studies as part of the final report) will be developed to assess SUNCASA’s achievements in reaching selected outcomes. This assignment also requests an interim 2-pager communications product prepared to illustrate the early results and lessons from SUNCASA based on the evaluation, to support discussions at key events taking place in October/November 2026. Lastly, a shorter report will also be developed to showcase high-level results from the final report. Specifics regarding the assignment deliverables are provided in Section 3 of this RFP. The 2-pager has a specific objective, audience and timeline intended for distribution at the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP). This deliverable will be developed first based on validated high-level, available results, with the final report and derived version to be completed at the end of the assignment. Therefore, the assignment includes a total of three (3) written deliverables, as outlined in Section 7 of this RFP. Appendix A presents the list of outcomes to be evaluated and proposed evaluation questions. The consultancy team is expected to review and revise the evaluation questions in collaboration with the IISD team prior to finalizing the evaluation. As the SUNCASA project has existing quantitative and qualitative data sources, the consultancy team can use existing SUNCASA data as secondary data sources. title: Construction Foreman
description: Position: Construction Foreman Employment Category: Permanent Location: Uganda Position Summary The Construction Foreman is the frontline leader responsible for supervising the labor crew and coordinating daily site activities. The role focuses on ensuring high productivity, maintaining safety standards on the ground, effective resource management, and reporting technical issues to the Site Engineer. He/ She ensures that construction tasks are completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project requirements. Major Duties & Responsibilities Lead, supervise and coordinate a multi-disciplinary team including subcontractors, masons, carpenters, steel fixers, plumbers, electricians, machine operators, and general laborers. Assign daily tasks based on the Site Engineer’s schedule and monitor quality control, work output and adherence to timelines. Enforce strict safety protocols: ensure 100% PPE usage, conduct weekly toolbox talks, and enforce permit-to-work systems. Manage site logistics: including material handling and work sequencing, ensure proper handling, storage, and efficient use of materials (cement, aggregates, steel) to minimize waste. Identify and report material shortages, equipment breakdowns, or safety hazards to the Site Engineer immediately. Maintain daily attendance records and manage overtime for daily wage workers. Coordinate with Electricians and Plumbers to avoid delays and ensure proper sequencing of trade (e.g., conduits and chases before casting). Report daily progress, manpower, and material usage to the Site Engineer. Identify and resolve on‑site challenges affecting workflow. Ensure proper use and maintenance of tools, machinery, and equipment. Complete any project related task assigned to him by the site engineer. Perform any additional related tasks as assigned by supervisors or management. About You Education & Experience Diploma or Certificate in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related trade. Minimum 5 years of field experience in civil construction as a Foreman or Leadman. AutoCAD or ArchiCAD certification is a strong advantage. Ability to read construction drawings and basic surveying; strong knowledge of local construction methods and structural finishes. Strong understanding of construction methods, safety standards, and site operations. Strong leadership, conflict resolution, and team motivation abilities. Core Competencies Practical and hands-on problem-solving. Excellent time management and delegation skills. High integrity in handling company assets and materials. Leadership and supervision Planning, organizing and time management Safety compliance Teamwork and communication
